title: Werewolf where every other player is an LLM with a secret role — what it took to make them bluff without giving themselves away
author: rezakhan0
selftext:
I built ***Lantern and Moon***, a browser werewolf/mafia game where you're one of 6–12 players and the rest are AI with secret roles. The whole challenge was one question: how do you get a model to keep a secret and lie about it, while the same model plays the honest villagers?



Three things made the difference. Each AI player is its own call with its own role, persona and memory, so they argue instead of agreeing. The werewolves only see what a real player would see, because a model given the night's secrets finds a way to mention them. And the players are told they're people at a table, not characters in a story — most of what gave the AI away was never a lie, it was stage directions and talking like a narrator.



Two more lessons. Voices matter more than I expected; the same game as text felt like reading a log. And efficiency is the real bottleneck for GenAI in games; so latency and cost per turn decide what the game can be, not the model's cleverness.



Free to play, no sign-up: [https://aibricks.io/wolf?code=J7443UUT&src=aigd](https://aibricks.io/wolf?code=J7443UUT&src=aigd)



Curious how others handle hidden information with a model that's also a player — and whether the AI fooled you.
